newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADIAN SPOT NATGAS PRICES RISE AMID TIGHT SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN SPOT NATGAS PRICES RISE AMID TIGHT SUPPLY.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices climbed on Wednesday as supply in Alberta again tightened after the long weekend, trading sources said.
"The day market is up. NOVA field receipts have dwindled from the weekend," a Calgary-based marketer said.
Field receipts on the NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd intra-Alberta pipeline system fell to 11.77 billion cubic feet a day on Tuesday from 12.3 BCFD on Monday. the marketer said.
The cut in available gas pushed the AECO spot price on Wednesday to about C$1.45 per gigajoule, up five to six cents from Tuesday. Last week's AECO spot price was C$1.50 per GJ.
September AECO was talked at C$1.42, up two cents from Tuesday, while the September-October term was pegged at an unchanged C$1.46 per GJ.

The marketer said forecast cooler temperatures in Alberta over the remainder of the week were expected to mean more available gas on the system and an accompanying drop in prices, likely back into the low C$1.40s.

Maintenace work on the Great Lakes Gas Transmission system to the U.S. Midwest from southern Manitoba was backing about 200 million cubic feet of gas a day into Alberta at Empress, but virtually all of it was being absorbed at the Alberta-British Columbia border point for export to sweltering California, traders said.
In the British Columbia market, prices were nearly flat with Tuesday, marketers said.
Sumas, Wash. spot gas was discussed in the US$1.05/1.07 per million British thermal unit range, unchanged from Tuesday but up from the low US$0.90s last week.
Sumas has rose this week along with Pacific Northwest and California border prices as West Coast temperatures and electricity prices climbed.
In the east, Dawn and Niagara in southern Ontario were unchanged to slightly higher at US$2.45/2.50 per mmBtu,
"Most of the activity is being done at Dawn and I think that is being driven by storage players," a trader with a large marketing firm said. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
